De-identification profiles

Source: R/anon_profile.R
anon_profile.Rd

A profile tells anon_deidentify() what each variable is: a direct identifier to remove, the subject key and related IDs, a date to offset, a quasi-identifier with its generalization ladder, a variable derived from a quasi-identifier, or a variable to keep. anon_profile_sdtm() and anon_profile_adam() describe standard CDISC SDTM and ADaM variables; anon_profile() and anon_profile_rule() build a profile for other data, or rules to add to a standard one with anon_profile_combine().

Usage

anon_profile(..., name = "custom")

anon_profile_rule(
  variable,
  role,
  datasets = character(0),
  quasi_name = NULL,
  test_col = NULL,
  test = NULL,
  flag = NULL,
  ladder = list(),
  from = character(0),
  priority = NA_integer_
)

anon_profile_sdtm(min_n = 12)

anon_profile_adam(min_n = 12)

anon_profile_combine(...)

# S3 method for class 'anon_profile'
c(...)

# S3 method for class 'anon_profile'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

...

For anon_profile(): rules made by anon_profile_rule(), profiles, or data frames with the columns of a profile (as as.data.frame() returns them), in order.

name

A name for the profile, shown when it is printed and in warnings when profiles are combined.

variable

Names of the variables the rule applies to: an exact name ("AGE"), an SDTM domain wildcard where -- stands for the two-letter domain prefix, in capitals ("--DTC" matches VSDTC and LBDTC, "--STDTC" matches AESTDTC and RFSTDTC, "--DY" matches VSDY but not body), or a pattern with * (any characters) and ? (one character), such as "*DT". Several names make one rule each, sharing the other arguments. For a test (test_col given), the result column ("VSSTRESN", "AVAL").

role

What the variable is:

  • "remove": a direct identifier, blanked in every row (the column is kept, with its type and attributes, so code that uses it still runs);

  • "key", "also", "key_cols": the subject key and related identifier columns, passed to anon_subject_ids() as key, also and key_cols;

  • "date": a date offset per subject by anon_subject_dates();

  • "quasi": a quasi-identifier, measured, generalized up its ladder and suppressed;

  • "derived": a variable derived from the quasi-identifiers in from, kept where it still follows from their released values and blanked elsewhere (see anon_deidentify());

  • "duration": a duration from the date in from to the date in variable, measured among the residual signals (see anon_quasi_duration()) and not changed;

  • "keep": kept as it is.

datasets

Names of the datasets the rule is limited to, exact or patterns with * and ? (such as "ad*"). Default: every dataset.

quasi_name

For "quasi" rules, the name of the quasi-identifier. Rules with the same name are copies of one quasi-identifier: such as baseline weight in SDTM vs, in ADaM WEIGHTBL and in advs. A quasi-identifier is measured from its source (see anon_deidentify()), generalized at the same level in every copy, and blanked for the same subjects in every copy. Default: test for a test, otherwise variable.

test_col, test

For a quasi-identifier or derived variable held in the rows of a test, such as baseline weight in vs: the column holding test codes ("VSTESTCD", "PARAMCD") and the test code ("WEIGHT"), or a pattern of test codes with * and ? ("RACE*", each code found being a copy of its own). variable is then the result column.

flag

For a test quasi-identifier, the column flagging the baseline record ("VSBLFL", "ABLFL"; "Y" marks it). The measured value is the subject's first flagged result, or, for a subject without a flagged result (or a dataset without the column), its first result. Every row of the test is generalized and blanked, not only the measured one.

ladder

For a quasi-identifier, its generalization ladder: a list of rules (anon_band(), anon_round(), anon_fold()), from the finest to the coarsest, each applied to the original values; the string "remove", as the last step, blanks the quasi-identifier in every row. An empty list: the quasi-identifier can only be suppressed. For a duration, one anon_band() giving the width of its bands in days.

from

For a derived variable, the names of the quasi-identifiers it is derived from; for a duration, the start date column.

priority

For a quasi-identifier, its usefulness, used to break ties when cells are suppressed (passed to anon_suppress() as order) and in the ladder search: between options that are otherwise equal, a lower number is blanked first. It doesn't decide what is blanked when one option blanks fewer cells. Quasi-identifiers without one follow, in profile order.

min_n

For the standard profiles, the smallest number of subjects a category must hold to be kept by their anon_fold() steps (RACE, the race qualifiers of SUPPDM, SITEID). Default 12, the group size the default target of anon_deidentify() (max_risk = 0.09) requires; set it to the group size of your target.

x

A profile.

row.names, optional

Not used.

Value

An object of class "anon_profile"; for anon_profile_rule(), a profile holding the rules.

Details

Structure. A profile is a tibble of rules with class "anon_profile" and columns variable, datasets (a list of character vectors, empty for every dataset), role, quasi_name, test_col, test, flag, ladder (a list of lists of rules), from (a list of character vectors), priority and profile (the name of the profile the rule came from). as.data.frame() returns it as a data frame to edit, and anon_profile() turns an edited data frame back into a profile.

Which rule applies. For a column of a dataset, among the rules (other than test rules) whose variable and datasets match it, a rule limited to datasets wins over one that isn't, an exact name over a pattern, and a later rule over an earlier one. Variable and dataset names and patterns are matched ignoring case ("RACE" matches race), except the domain prefix that -- stands for, which is two capital letters. Test rules apply to the rows of their test in every dataset (in datasets) with the test and result columns.

Companion variables. ADaM names a variable's numeric code XN and its decoded or long label XL or XC (SITEIDN, COUNTRYL, USUBJIDN). anon_deidentify() gives the companions of the key and of each "also" column the "also" role (a numeric companion gets the number of the subject's pseudonym, 31 for SUBJ-031, the same in every dataset), and makes the companions of each quasi-identifier column "derived" from it. A rule that matches a companion's name wins, in the datasets it covers.

Columns matched by no rule are kept as they are, except that dates are offset and subject IDs replaced wherever anon_subject_dates() and anon_subject_ids() find them. anon_deidentify() warns about columns, at any depth, whose names look like an age, a birth date (*BRTH*, *BIRTH*, DOB*), a site, a numeric ID (*IDN), a country (COUNTRY*, CNTRY*), a ZIP or postal code (ZIP*, POSTAL*), a sex or gender, a race (RACE1, RACEOTH), an ethnicity, a height (HT, HTS too), a weight (WT, WTS, BW, BWT too), a BMI, a body surface area, a creatinine clearance or an eGFR, in any case (units, named *U, aside), and that no rule matches, unless they hold no value, or one value (and no other factor level, value label or missing-value code) that at least as many subjects as the target's group size share; such a column is a reason the target is not met. So is an element of a list column (a plain list or vector held in it, at any depth) named like one, or matched by a rule other than "keep". It also warns about "keep" rules that win over a quasi-identifier's rule for a column.

Datasets without the key. A dataset without the key column whose every row holds, in its "also" columns (such as SUBJID, or USUBJIDN), a value that the datasets with the key give one subject, and no value that points to no subject, to several or to another subject, is processed as a dataset with the key (rows tied to those subjects) and released without the key column. Any other dataset without the key that holds a column matched by a "key", "also", "key_cols", "quasi", "derived", "date" or "duration" rule, or that looks like a quasi-identifier, is released as it is and is a reason the target is not met. A codelist or lookup table without the key (such as a format table holding SEX and SEXN, or age bands with AGEGR1) holds no subject's values: keep it knowingly with a "keep" rule limited to that dataset, such as anon_profile_rule(c("SEX", "SEXN"), "keep", datasets = "fmt") combined with the profile. The rule then applies only there.

Dates. anon_deidentify() offsets dates with anon_subject_dates()'s own detection (every Date and date-time column and every text column whose name ends in DTC, at any depth), and, with the same offsets, the text columns of ISO 8601 dates matched by a "date" or "duration" rule (such as VISIT_DATE), at any depth. A column matched by such a rule that isn't a Date, a date-time or text (a number of days, with or without a SAS date format, whose origin isn't known) is left as it is: a warning names it, and it is a reason the target is not met.

anon_profile_sdtm().

  • remove: BRTHDTC (with AGE and an offset RFSTDTC, a birth date gives the age back exactly, even after offsetting, and a birth year undoes AGE bands, so it is removed rather than reduced to the year), INVNAM, INVID;

  • key USUBJID, also SUBJID, key_cols RSUBJID;

  • dates: --DTC, --STDTC, --ENDTC and every other *DTC;

  • quasi-identifiers, each with its ladder: AGE (5-, 10- and 20-year bands, ages of 90 and over as 90), SEX (suppressed only), RACE (categories of fewer than min_n subjects folded into "OTHER", a CDISC controlled term), ETHNIC (suppressed only: its controlled terminology has no neutral other value), SITEID (small sites merged into "OTHER", then removed), COUNTRY (removed: ISO 3166 has no code for "other", so a small country can't be folded), the race qualifiers of SUPPDM (QVAL where QNAM is RACE*: copies of RACE, folded alike), and baseline HEIGHT and WEIGHT from vs (VSSTRESN with VSORRES and VSSTRESC; flag VSBLFL, else the first record: height is often recorded once, at screening, without the flag), rounded to units, then to tens, then in bands of 20;

  • derived: BMI and BSA results in vs, from HEIGHT and WEIGHT (blanked where those changed); renal function results in lb (CRCL, EGFR) are not covered: add derived rules for them if needed;

  • duration: RFSTDTC to RFENDTC, in bands of 7 days;

  • keep: AGEU (the unit of AGE, not identifying), --DY, --STDY and --ENDY (study days, which offsetting keeps exact).

Priorities (ties are broken by blanking first): SITEID, COUNTRY, ETHNIC, RACE, HEIGHT, WEIGHT, AGE, SEX.

The AGE ladder doesn't follow a study's age groups (such as AGEGR1 cut at 65): where a band straddles a cut, the group is blanked. To keep them, combine the profile with an AGE rule whose ladder uses bands that align with the cuts, such as anon_band(5, bottom = 15) for cuts at 65 (AAGE in ADaM takes its own rule).

anon_profile_adam(). Rules match ADSL variables in every dataset that carries them (ADSL, BDS and OCCDS datasets alike).

  • remove: BRTHDT, BRTHDTM, BRTHDTC, INVNAM, INVID;

  • key, also and key_cols as for SDTM;

  • dates: *DT, *DTM and *DTC (such as TRTSDT, TRTEDT, RANDDT, ADT, ADTM);

  • quasi-identifiers: AGE (with AAGE, the age at an event, as a copy), SEX, RACE, ETHNIC, SITEID and COUNTRY as for SDTM; EDUCLVL (suppressed only); HEIGHT and WEIGHT as copies in HEIGHTBL/HTBL/HGTBL and WEIGHTBL/WTBL/WGTBL, in the AVAL of their PARAMCD rows (flag ABLFL; AVALC, BASE, BASEC, CHG, PCHG and R2BASE follow, see anon_rule()) and in the SDTM results (VSSTRESN) that BDS datasets carry, with the SDTM ladders;

  • derived: RACEN, RACEGR* from RACE; SEXN from SEX; ETHNICN from ETHNIC; AGEGR* (such as AGEGR1 and AGEGR1N) from AGE; AAGEGR* from AAGE; REGION* from COUNTRY; SITEGR* from SITEID; BMIBL and BMIBLGR* from HEIGHT and WEIGHT; BSA* (such as BSABL) from HEIGHT and WEIGHT, and CRCL* and EGFR* (CRCLBL, EGFRBL) from HEIGHT, WEIGHT, AGE and SEX, their units (*U) kept; AVALCAT* and AVALCA*N of the HEIGHT and WEIGHT rows from them; the BMI and BSA parameters, from HEIGHT and WEIGHT; and the CRCL and EGFR parameters (renal function in a BDS dataset such as ADLB), from HEIGHT, WEIGHT, AGE and SEX;

  • duration: TRTSDT to TRTEDT, in bands of 7 days.

Columns that hold a duration exactly, such as TRTDURD, ADURN or --DUR, and study days (ADY, --DY) are kept: offsetting doesn't change them, and they can single subjects out like the durations measured among the residual signals. Remove them if that matters.

In BDS datasets, results (AVAL, AVALC, BASE, BASEC, CHG, PCHG, R2BASE) are not quasi-identifiers, except for the baseline height and weight parameters: a lab value or a blood pressure is not something an attacker would know. Add rules for other parameters that are.

Combining. anon_profile_combine() (or c()) joins profiles, such as the SDTM and ADaM profiles for a list holding both. A rule of a later profile replaces a rule of an earlier one with the same variable, datasets, test_col and test (in its place); a replacement with another role is named in a warning. Quasi-identifiers with the same name are one quasi-identifier: one set of generalizations, applied to every copy.

See also

anon_deidentify()

Examples

anon_profile_sdtm()
#> <anon_profile> sdtm: 26 rule(s)
#> 
#> remove:
#>   INVNAM
#>   INVID
#>   BRTHDTC
#> 
#> key:
#>   USUBJID
#> 
#> also:
#>   SUBJID
#> 
#> key_cols:
#>   RSUBJID
#> 
#> date:
#>   --DTC
#>   --STDTC
#>   --ENDTC
#>   *DTC
#> 
#> quasi:
#>   AGE, ladder: anon_band(width = 5, top = 90) > anon_band(width = 10, top = 90) > anon_band(width = 20, top = 90), priority 7
#>   SEX, suppressed only, priority 8
#>   RACE, ladder: anon_fold(min_n = 12, to = "OTHER"), priority 4
#>   ETHNIC, suppressed only, priority 3
#>   SITEID, ladder: anon_fold(min_n = 12, to = "OTHER") > remove, priority 1
#>   COUNTRY, ladder: remove, priority 2
#>   VSSTRESN where VSTESTCD = HEIGHT, baseline flag VSBLFL, ladder: anon_round(digits = 0) > anon_round(digits = -1) > anon_band(width = 20), priority 5
#>   VSSTRESN where VSTESTCD = WEIGHT, baseline flag VSBLFL, ladder: anon_round(digits = 0) > anon_round(digits = -1) > anon_band(width = 20), priority 6
#>   QVAL where QNAM = RACE* in supp* (copy of RACE), ladder: anon_fold(min_n = 12, to = "OTHER"), priority 4
#> 
#> derived:
#>   VSSTRESN where VSTESTCD = BMI, from HEIGHT, WEIGHT
#>   VSSTRESN where VSTESTCD = BSA, from HEIGHT, WEIGHT
#> 
#> duration:
#>   RFENDTC, ladder: anon_band(width = 7), from RFSTDTC
#> 
#> keep:
#>   AGEU
#>   --DY
#>   --STDY
#>   --ENDY

# A profile for data that isn't CDISC: a key, a date and two
# quasi-identifiers.
anon_profile(
  anon_profile_rule("ID", "key"),
  anon_profile_rule("VISIT_DATE", "date"),
  anon_profile_rule("AGE", "quasi", ladder = list(anon_band(10, top = 90))),
  anon_profile_rule("SEX", "quasi"),
  name = "registry"
)
#> <anon_profile> registry: 4 rule(s)
#> 
#> key:
#>   ID
#> 
#> date:
#>   VISIT_DATE
#> 
#> quasi:
#>   AGE, ladder: anon_band(width = 10, top = 90)
#>   SEX, suppressed only

# The SDTM and ADaM profiles together, for a list holding both.
c(anon_profile_sdtm(), anon_profile_adam())
#> <anon_profile> sdtm + adam: 65 rule(s)
#> 
#> remove:
#>   INVNAM
#>   INVID
#>   BRTHDTC
#>   BRTHDT
#>   BRTHDTM
#> 
#> key:
#>   USUBJID
#> 
#> also:
#>   SUBJID
#> 
#> key_cols:
#>   RSUBJID
#> 
#> date:
#>   --DTC
#>   --STDTC
#>   --ENDTC
#>   *DTC
#>   *DT
#>   *DTM
#> 
#> quasi:
#>   AGE, ladder: anon_band(width = 5, top = 90) > anon_band(width = 10, top = 90) > anon_band(width = 20, top = 90), priority 7
#>   SEX, suppressed only, priority 8
#>   RACE, ladder: anon_fold(min_n = 12, to = "OTHER"), priority 4
#>   ETHNIC, suppressed only, priority 3
#>   SITEID, ladder: anon_fold(min_n = 12, to = "OTHER") > remove, priority 1
#>   COUNTRY, ladder: remove, priority 2
#>   VSSTRESN where VSTESTCD = HEIGHT, baseline flag VSBLFL, ladder: anon_round(digits = 0) > anon_round(digits = -1) > anon_band(width = 20), priority 5
#>   VSSTRESN where VSTESTCD = WEIGHT, baseline flag VSBLFL, ladder: anon_round(digits = 0) > anon_round(digits = -1) > anon_band(width = 20), priority 6
#>   QVAL where QNAM = RACE* in supp* (copy of RACE), ladder: anon_fold(min_n = 12, to = "OTHER"), priority 4
#>   AAGE (copy of AGE), ladder: anon_band(width = 5, top = 90) > anon_band(width = 10, top = 90) > anon_band(width = 20, top = 90), priority 7
#>   EDUCLVL, suppressed only, priority 3
#>   HEIGHTBL (copy of HEIGHT), ladder: anon_round(digits = 0) > anon_round(digits = -1) > anon_band(width = 20), priority 5
#>   HTBL (copy of HEIGHT), ladder: anon_round(digits = 0) > anon_round(digits = -1) > anon_band(width = 20), priority 5
#>   HGTBL (copy of HEIGHT), ladder: anon_round(digits = 0) > anon_round(digits = -1) > anon_band(width = 20), priority 5

#>   VSSTRESN where VSTESTCD = BMI, from HEIGHT, WEIGHT

#>   RACEGR*, from RACE

#>   ETHNICN, from ETHNIC
#>   AGEGR*, from AGE
#>   AAGEGR*, from AAGE
#>   REGION*, from COUNTRY
